about.title: About AeroLex
about.lead: AeroLex wants to be an interactive aviation reference: part academy, part technical dictionary, part encyclopedia and part tool lab, fully in English and Spanish.
audience: People discovering aviation for the first time
Student pilots and pilots who want to go further
Cabin crew in training and in service
AvGeeks who want to recognise every aircraft
Anyone who wants to read METARs and TAFs or improve their aviation English

principles.bilingual: Everything in both languages: lessons, definitions, quizzes and tools. Standard English terms such as METAR, QNH or MAYDAY are kept and explained.
principles.sources: Nothing invented: data, regulations and procedures come from official, cited sources.
principles.differences: European (EASA) and US (FAA) differences are pointed out.
principles.educational: Educational, not operational. The operator's approved manuals and procedures always prevail.

sources: Regulations and standards: ICAO, EU/EASA, FAA, WMO
Official training publications: FAA handbooks, AIP Spain (ENAIRE), AEMET
Manufacturers' public documentation: Airbus, Boeing, ATR, Embraer…
Official accident investigation bodies: CIAIAC, BEA, NTSB, AAIB…
about.openText: AeroLex is developed publicly on GitHub, phase by phase. You can follow the progress, read the documentation or report an error.

legal.title: Legal notice & privacy
legal.educationalText: The content and tools on AeroLex are for educational purposes. They do not replace approved training, the aircraft flight manual (AFM/POH), the operator's operations manual, aeronautical information publications or any current official documentation. They must not be used for flight planning or real operations.
privacy: AeroLex uses no cookies and no analytics or tracking tools.
Your progress and preferences are stored only in your browser (LocalStorage). You can export or delete them at any time from the dashboard.
Fonts are served from this site, not from third-party font services.
The site is hosted on GitHub Pages; GitHub may process technical data such as your IP address to serve it, under its own privacy statement.
legal.accuracyText: We work to cite official sources and show the review status of every entry. If you find an error, please report it on GitHub.
legal.licenceText: The licences for the code and the content will be published before version 1.0. Third-party images and data keep their own licences and attribution.

styleguide.title: Design system
styleguide.lead: The tokens and reusable components AeroLex is built from. Every section of the platform uses only what appears here.
styleguide.coloursText: The semantic colours follow the logic of flight deck displays: red for warnings, amber for cautions, green for normal, cyan for selectable items and magenta for targets and the active route. Every text/background pair meets WCAG AA contrast.
styleguide.sampleText: Lift is the aerodynamic force that acts perpendicular to the relative airflow.
styleguide.calloutInfo: Information: context that helps understand the topic.
styleguide.calloutTip: Tip: a practical way to remember or apply it.
styleguide.calloutCaution: Caution: a common mistake or a nuance to watch.
styleguide.calloutWarning: Warning: something that matters for safety.
styleguide.calloutRegional: EASA/FAA difference: Europe and ICAO report pressure in hPa (Q1013); the US uses inches of mercury (A2992).
styleguide.calloutOfficial: Official procedure: this is educational material. The operator's approved procedures always prevail.
styleguide.cardText: Used for courses: origin and destination are your starting and target level.
styleguide.tabAirbusText: Airbus fly-by-wire airliners (from the A320 family onward) use sidesticks and the ECAM system to display engine data and alerts.
styleguide.tabBoeingText: Boeing airliners keep control columns (yokes), including the fly-by-wire 777 and 787. The 757, 767, 747-400, 777 and 787 use EICAS; the 737 does not use a full EICAS.
styleguide.accordionQ: Why are aviation terms kept in English?
styleguide.accordionA: English is the common working language of international aviation. Keeping terms like METAR or QNH avoids translations that a pilot or controller would not recognise.
styleguide.modalText: Dialogs can be closed with the Escape key, the close button or by clicking outside.

hangar.metaDescription: Aircraft families and variants with figures taken from manufacturers' official documentation, and a comparator.
hangar.title: Hangar
hangar.lead: An aircraft encyclopedia where every figure comes from the manufacturer's official documentation. Each variant has its own figures, because no 'A320' or '737' is generic.
hangar.notPublished: Not published in the cited sources
hangar.dataNote: Figures as published by the manufacturer in the cited sources. A dash (—) means the cited source does not give that value; we never estimate it.
hangar.compareLead: Choose two or three variants to compare them side by side. The highest known value for each figure is highlighted.
hangar.compareEmpty: Choose at least two variants to compare.
hangar.educational: Educational tool. Figures are generic manufacturer data; actual aircraft vary by operator, configuration and engine. Not for operational use.

type.SPECI: Special report: issued between routine reports when conditions change significantly.
type.TAF: Terminal aerodrome forecast (TAF). Use the TAF decoder to read it.

modifier.COR: Corrected report: replaces an earlier one that had an error.
modifier.AUTO: Automated observation, with no human intervention.
modifier.NIL: Missing report: there is no data for this time.

explain.station: ICAO location indicator of the aerodrome: {code}.
explain.time: Day {day} of the month, at {hh}:{mm} UTC.
explain.windVariation: The wind direction varies between {from}° and {to}°.
explain.cavok: CAVOK: visibility 10 km or more, no cloud below 5,000 ft (or the highest minimum sector altitude, if greater), no cumulonimbus or towering cumulus, and no significant weather.
explain.visNdv: NDV: the automated station cannot assess directional variations.
explain.wxVicinity: {what} in the vicinity of the aerodrome, not at it
explain.wxNsw: NSW: no significant weather (end of significant weather)
explain.recent: Recent weather, observed since the previous report but no longer present: {what}.
explain.clouds: {cover} with the base at {h} ft above the aerodrome.
explain.vvMissing: Sky obscured; vertical visibility not available.

special.NSC: NSC: no significant cloud (none below 5,000 ft and no cumulonimbus or towering cumulus).
special.NCD: NCD: the automated station detects no cloud.
special.CLR: CLR: the automated station detects no cloud below 12,000 ft (US usage).

trend.NOSIG: NOSIG: no significant change expected in the next 2 hours.
trend.BECMG: BECMG: a change expected to happen gradually.

explain.remarks: National remarks. Shown as they are: not decoded.
explain.unknown: Group not recognised. It is not interpreted, to avoid misleading you.
explain.invalidNote: ⚠ Recognised format, but with impossible values.

issues.empty: Type or paste a METAR or SPECI message.
issues.isTaf: This looks like a TAF, not a METAR.
issues.noStation: The aerodrome ICAO location indicator is missing.
issues.noTime: The day and time group (DDHHMMZ) is missing.
issues.noVisibility: No visibility group or CAVOK was found.
issues.noTemperature: No temperature and dew point group was found.
issues.noPressure: No pressure group (Q or A) was found.
issues.cavokWithWeather: CAVOK should not be accompanied by present weather or cloud groups.
issues.outOfOrder: Group {group} is out of the usual order.
issues.windNotTens: The wind direction in {group} is not rounded to the nearest ten degrees.

invalid.range: Group {group} has values out of range.
invalid.gust: In {group}, the gust cannot be less than or equal to the mean wind.
invalid.dewAboveTemp: In {group}, the dew point cannot be higher than the temperature.

metarTool.metaDescription: Decode a METAR or SPECI group by group, in English and Spanish, in ICAO and US formats.
metarTool.title: METAR decoder
metarTool.lead: Paste a METAR or SPECI and every group is explained in plain language. It handles ICAO and US formats (SM, inHg, RMK) and flags what it does not recognise instead of guessing.
metarTool.hint: It decodes as you type. The message never leaves your browser.
metarTool.tableCaption: Explanation of each group in the message
metarTool.noscript: The decoder needs JavaScript. Below is an example that has already been decoded.
metarTool.learnMore: Want to learn to read it yourself? Try the METAR and SPECI Academy.

explain.validity: Valid from day {d1} at {h1}:00 UTC to day {d2} at {h2}:00 UTC ({hours} hours).
explain.changeFM: FM: from day {day} at {hh}:{mm} UTC, completely new conditions begin; everything before stops applying.
explain.BECMG: BECMG: the elements that follow change gradually during the period and remain afterwards.
explain.TEMPO: TEMPO: temporary fluctuations; each lasts less than an hour and, in total, less than half the period.
explain.PROB: PROB{p}: a {p} % probability of the conditions that follow.
explain.PROBTEMPO: PROB{p} TEMPO: a {p} % probability of temporary fluctuations with the conditions that follow.
explain.changePeriod: From day {d1} at {h1}:00 to day {d2} at {h2}:00 UTC.
explain.TX: Forecast maximum temperature: {v} °C, on day {day} at {hh}:00 UTC.
explain.TN: Forecast minimum temperature: {v} °C, on day {day} at {hh}:00 UTC.
explain.type: Terminal aerodrome forecast (TAF): the conditions expected at the aerodrome during the validity period.

issues.notTaf: This looks like a METAR or SPECI, not a TAF. Use the METAR decoder.
issues.validityLength: The validity is {hours} hours; ICAO sets it between 6 and 30 hours.
issues.becmgTooLong: The period in {group} is longer than 4 hours, the maximum for BECMG.
issues.outsideValidity: The change {group} falls outside the validity period.
issues.periodReversed: In {group}, the end of the period is before its start.
issues.noChangePeriod: The DDHH/DDHH period is missing after {group}.

invalid.prob: In {group}: ICAO only uses PROB30 and PROB40.

1.title: Level 1 · Identify the group
1.text: What kind of information does each group give?

2.title: Level 2 · Read the value
2.text: What exactly does the highlighted group mean?

3.title: Level 3 · Full METAR
3.text: Ceiling, present weather, temperature and trend.

4.title: Level 4 · TAF
4.text: Forecast conditions, change groups and validity.

practice.saved: Your history at this level: {correct} right and {wrong} wrong.

prompts.identify: What information does the highlighted group ({group}) give?
prompts.meaning: What does the highlighted group ({group}) mean?
prompts.ceiling: What is the ceiling (the lowest BKN or OVC layer, or the vertical visibility)?
prompts.spread: What is the difference between temperature and dew point?
prompts.trend: What does the report say about the next 2 hours?
prompts.tafWind: Overall (not counting TEMPO or PROB), what wind is expected on day {day} at {hh}:{mm} UTC?
prompts.tafVisibility: Overall (not counting TEMPO or PROB), what visibility is expected on day {day} at {hh}:{mm} UTC?
prompts.change: What does the highlighted group ({group}) indicate?
prompts.validityEnd: When does this TAF's validity end?

change.FM: From that time, completely new conditions

explain.ceiling: The ceiling is the base of the lowest BKN or OVC layer, or the vertical visibility (VV). FEW and SCT do not form a ceiling.
explain.noWeather: The report has no present weather group.
explain.spreadSmall: A difference of 2 °C or less means the air is almost saturated: fog or mist are possible.
explain.spreadLarge: With a large difference, the air is far from saturation.
explain.tafPrevailing: The prevailing conditions come from the base, the FM groups and any BECMG already completed; TEMPO and PROB are temporary or possible.

converter.metaDescription: Convert speed, distance, altitude, mass, pressure, volume and temperature between the units used in aviation.
converter.title: Unit converter
converter.lead: The units that get mixed up most in aviation, converted instantly: type a value in any field and the others update.

notes.speed: 1 kt = 1 NM per hour = exactly 1.852 km/h.
notes.pressure: 1 inHg = 33.8639 hPa; ISA at sea level is 1013.25 hPa = 29.92 inHg.
notes.volume: Volume, not mass: converting to kg needs the fuel density, which changes with temperature.

live.metaDescription: The latest METAR and TAF for a selection of airports, decoded, with the issue time and a warning when data is old.
live.title: Live METAR and TAF
live.lead: The latest METAR and TAF for a selection of airports, downloaded automatically from the Aviation Weather Center (NOAA/NWS) and decoded on the spot.
live.warning: Real data, but for educational purposes only: not for operational use. Downloads are periodic and may be delayed; for flying, always use official aviation weather services.
live.updates: Updated roughly every 30 minutes; scheduled GitHub runs can be delayed.
live.noData: There is no live data available right now. You can paste any METAR or TAF into the decoders.
live.fetchErrors: The last download had problems, so some data may be missing.
live.noMetar: No METAR in the last download.
live.noTaf: No TAF in the last download (not every aerodrome issues TAFs).
live.source: Source: Aviation Weather Center (NOAA/NWS), US public domain data.
live.otherAirport: Another airport? Paste its METAR or TAF into the decoder.

atc.metaDescription: Practise reading back ATC clearances as a pilot and spotting read-back errors as a controller, with didactic scenarios.
atc.title: ATC phraseology trainer
atc.lead: Practise read-backs with complete didactic scenarios in English, the usual language of aviation radio. As a pilot, type the read-back; as a controller, spot the errors.
atc.fictitious: Didactic scenario: the LEXAIR call sign, the ROSAL 1A departure and the frequencies are fictitious.
atc.placeholder: Type your read-back in English, in words or figures
atc.callsignNotLast: Tip: the call sign goes at the end of the read-back.
atc.readbackRule: Under SERA.8015(e) and ICAO PANS-ATM, these are always read back: route clearances; instructions to enter, land on, take off from, hold short of, cross, taxi on or backtrack on a runway; runway in use, altimeter settings, SSR codes, new frequencies, level, heading and speed instructions, and transition levels. "Roger" or "Wilco" never replace a read-back.
atc.noSpeech: Your browser cannot read the message aloud.
